title: Reveal-faded chip hairline violates the pinned full-alpha rlsw line-alpha trap (DrawRectangleLinesEx alpha < 255)
evidence:
// the paper chip + ink hairline (full-alpha — the rlsw line-alpha trap)
	paper := v.palette.canvas
	paper.a = u8(f32(paper.a) * fade)
	rl.DrawRectangleV({x0, y0}, {cw, ch}, paper)
	out := v.palette.ink_soft
	out.a = u8(255 * fade)
	rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx({x0, y0, cw, ch}, max(1.0, s * 0.02 * reveal_scale), out)
detail: During reveal windows fade ∈ [0.3,1), so the hairline draws at alpha < 255. Per the project's own pinned trap (spawn_fx.odin: "line alpha is ignored" in rlsw), goldens capture it solid while the GPU app blends — live-vs-capture divergence in the re-blessed spawn frames.
recommended_fix: Keep the hairline pinned out.a = 255 through the reveal (fade only the fills), or draw the outline as four alpha-blended filled rects like the ring annulus.

title: u64 wrap in T - SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS when the growth interval is below 10 silently suppresses the telegraph ring
evidence:
window := tick + u64(interval) - (tick % u64(interval))
...
	T := fx.telegraph.spawn_tick
	if tick < T - SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS || tick > T + SPAWN_BURST_TICKS {
detail: T is a multiple of interval; the catalog only enforces interval >= 1 ("must be >= 1 with all keys present"). At interval 1..9 the first window T < 10 wraps u64, tick < ~2^64 is always true, and the ring never draws.
recommended_fix: Compute the window start in i64 (age := i64(tick) - i64(T) + SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS; if age < 0 return), or reject terminal_spawn_interval_ticks <= SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS at catalog load.

title: interval - 5 u64 wrap in the predict test hangs the suite instead of failing when the catalog is zeroed or retuned below 5
detail: If catalogs_load fails (wrong cwd) interval is 0; interval - 5 wraps to ~2^64 and sfx_run's step loop runs ~forever — a hang, not a test failure. Also fires if the cadence knob retunes below 5.
recommended_fix: Guard before the subtraction: expect interval >= SPAWN_LEAD_TICKS + 5 and testing.errorf/return early, e.g. if interval < 15 { testing.errorf(t, ...); return }.

title: sfx_load_cat's read1 prints the os.read error then returns nil, dropping the error value (catch-and-ignore)
detail: The error value is discarded after printing; the tests then run against a zeroed catalog, so any failure reports misleading catalog symptoms (or the interval-wrap hang) instead of the IO cause.
recommended_fix: Return (b, ok) or track a failed flag; testing.errorf the read failure at the top of each test before touching the catalog.

title: spawn_fx_init/spawn_fx_destroy have no call sites — the reveals buffer grows unowned on the ambient allocator and is never freed
detail: grep over app/ and harness/ finds only spawn_fx_reset calls (app/main.odin:741, harness/run.odin:293). reveals is a zeroed [dynamic] grown on first append via the ambient context.allocator — the declared ownership/teardown pair is dead code.
recommended_fix: Either call spawn_fx_init at View creation and spawn_fx_destroy at teardown, or delete the dead procs and document that reveals rides append-on-nil with the ambient allocator.
